# Check catalogue

<!-- Generated by `preflight docs` from the check registry (ngs-preflight 0.1.0). Do not edit by hand; a test fails if this file is out of date. -->

This page lists all checks in ngs-preflight 0.1.0. Since it is generated from the same registry used by the tool at runtime, it cannot diverge from the code. To view an individual check in your terminal, run `preflight explain <ID>`.

## How to read this page

- **ERROR** indicates that the submission is likely to fail or return incorrect results. Correct the issue first.
- **WARN** indicates a possible issue or risk. Check the details. If `--strict` is specified, the warning is treated as an error.
- **INFO** is a note or summary and never affects the exit code.
- When a check is triggered, anything in `{braces}` in the message is filled in with values from your files.
- Exit codes of `preflight check`: `0` pass, `1` errors found (or warnings with `--strict`), `2` warnings only, `3` tool or usage error.

## Target regions (BED)

<a id="bed001"></a>
### BED001: BED file can be read

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} Tools which read this file will stop running or silently skip the affected lines. This may result in the loss of some target regions.

**How it works**

Except for header lines, each line must contain at least 3 tab-separated columns, and columns 2 and 3 must contain integers. Lines beginning with 'track', 'browser', or '#' are permitted header lines and are included in the line count (see BED009). Blank lines are ignored. Gzip-compressed BED files are decompressed first.

**Suggested fix**

> Open the file and edit or delete the listed lines. Each line must contain a chromosome name, start position, and end position separated by tabs. Start and end positions must be integers.

<a id="bed002"></a>
### BED002: Start and end make sense

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} {have} invalid coordinates (for example, line {line} starts at {start:,} and ends at {end:,}). Regions must start at 0 or greater and end after their start position. Empty regions or regions with reversed start and end positions are rejected or silently ignored by most tools.

**How it works**

All intervals must satisfy 0 <= start < end. BED uses 0-based, half-open intervals.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the start and end columns in the listed rows. If start and end have been swapped, restore their original order. You can remove empty regions where start and end are equal.

<a id="bed003"></a>
### BED003: Chromosome names exist in the reference

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** a reference (`--reference`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {summary} in the BED file cannot be found in the reference sequence: {contigs}. {hint} Tools will fail or skip these regions, so data you expect to be analyzed would be missing.

**How it works**

All contig names in column 1 are checked against sequence names in the reference .fai/.dict using case-sensitive exact matching. If adding or removing the 'chr' prefix (including MT <-> chrM) resolves all unmatched names, the message states this and suggests running 'preflight fix-bed'.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="bed004"></a>
### BED004: Intervals stay inside their chromosome

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** a reference (`--reference`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} {extend} beyond the end of {its} chromosome in the reference sequence (for example, line {line}, {contig} is {length:,} bp long, but the interval ends at {end:,}). This usually means that the BED was created for a different genome build or contains a typographical error.

**How it works**

For contigs present in the reference sequence, end must be less than or equal to the contig length recorded in .fai/.dict.

**Suggested fix**

> Please confirm that the BED was created for the same genome build as the reference sequence (for example, GRCh38, not GRCh37). If it was created for the same genome build, correct or remove the listed rows.

<a id="bed005"></a>
### BED005: Intervals are sorted

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> The BED file is not sorted: {reason}. Some commonly used tools (bedtools, tabix, and many variant callers) require sorted regions. If regions are not sorted, these tools will stop running or quietly return incorrect results.

**How it works**

Sorted means that each chromosome forms a single continuous block and start positions within each block do not decrease. These blocks follow reference sequence order (if a reference sequence is specified) or simple alphabetical order (the order produced by 'sort -k1,1 -k2,2n').

**Suggested fix**

> Run preflight fix-bed --sort <file> --out <sorted file>. To sort in reference sequence order, add --reference.

<a id="bed006"></a>
### BED006: No overlapping or touching intervals

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {what}. Summing the recorded intervals gives a total target size of {raw}, while coverage after merging overlaps is only {merged} ({before} regions become {after}). When overlaps are present, coverage can be counted more than once, and some tools may report the same region twice.

**How it works**

Intervals are sorted per chromosome. An interval overlaps if it starts before the furthest end seen so far. If its start position exactly matches that end position, the intervals are adjacent at their endpoints (book-ended). As in `bedtools merge`, merged territory is calculated after merging overlapping and book-ended intervals.

**Suggested fix**

> Run preflight fix-bed --merge <file> --out <merged file>, or remove duplicates manually.

<a id="bed007"></a>
### BED007: Coordinates look 0-based (heuristic)

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> This BED file may use coordinates starting at 1. This is a heuristic inference based on patterns in the file and is not certain ({reasons}). Since BED coordinates start at 0, all regions would be shifted by 1 base if this file actually uses coordinates starting at 1. This may result in 1 base being missing or added at each boundary.

**How it works**

This heuristic is deliberately conservative and detects only 1 type of evidence. Among adjacent, non-overlapping region pairs on a chromosome, at least 5 pairs must have a gap of exactly 1 base. Their number must also be at least 3 times the number of directly adjoining pairs. These pairs must account for at least 10% of all adjacent region pairs. If any region starts at 0, 1-based coordinates are ruled out and this check is silenced. Since this pattern is absent from lists of sparse target regions, most 1-based files cannot be detected.

**Suggested fix**

> Confirm how the file was generated. If coordinates came from a spreadsheet, a 1-based closed-interval export, or a VCF/GFF list, subtract 1 from the values in the start column. Leave the values in the end column unchanged. If you are certain that the file is a 0-based BED file, you can ignore this warning.

**Notes**

**Why a heuristic.** BED files do not specify their coordinate convention, and files with shifted coordinates are still valid BED files. Since only indirect evidence is available, this check looks for patterns which are relatively rare in files that actually use 0-based coordinates:

*Exactly-one-base gaps between neighbours.* Adjacent 0-based half-open intervals which cover a genomic segment without gaps share a boundary (the next interval starts where the previous interval ends). When the same region is represented by 1-based closed intervals, each interval starts exactly 1 position after the previous interval ends. Gaps of exactly 1 base rarely occur by chance (gaps between targets are typically tens to thousands of bases). Therefore, a file can be considered suspicious if it contains many such gaps and few intervals which meet directly at their boundaries.

*What is deliberately not used.* Coordinates recorded in the name column, such as `chr1:101-200` for a region starting at 100, cannot be used as evidence for either case.

Even when a file correctly uses 0-based coordinates, its names often use 1-based coordinates. In hastily created files, column values are used unchanged as names. Therefore, names cannot be used to distinguish between these cases.

In files using 1-based coordinates, `start` cannot be 0. Therefore, the check will report nothing if such intervals are present. Thresholds are fixed in the code (`ONE_BASED_MIN_EVIDENCE = 5` and the ratios above). This check produces false negatives by design.

Sparse interval lists, such as capture panels where exons are sufficiently far apart, have no identifiable pattern. Detecting these cases requires annotation information based on the positions where exons begin in known gene models. However, ngs-preflight does not include this information. Since the aim is to avoid false positives, the check reports nothing when it cannot be confident.

<a id="bed008"></a>
### BED008: Clean file formatting

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} {consequence}

**How it works**

Looks for UTF-8 byte order marks, CRLF (Windows) line endings, spaces used as column delimiters, and trailing spaces or tabs. Since the parser accepts all 4 cases, the remaining checks are still run on the cleaned content.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="bed009"></a>
### BED009: Territory summary

**Severity:** INFO. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {summary}

**How it works**

Counts intervals, total base pairs, base pairs after merging, and size distribution. Counts intervals on alt/decoy/unplaced contigs (contigs whose names do not match chr1-22, X, Y, or M, regardless of whether they include 'chr'). Also records whether chrY and chrM are present and the number of ignored header lines.

**Suggested fix**

> No action is required. Confirm that the totals match the expected values for your design (for example, the panel or exome you ordered).

<a id="bed010"></a>
### BED010: Interval sizes are plausible for a capture panel

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {what}. Extremely short regions often result from input errors where the start and end positions are nearly identical. Extremely long regions typically result from accidentally pasting an entire gene or chromosome. These types of regions behave differently from standard capture targets.

**How it works**

Flags intervals shorter than 20 bp and those longer than 1,000,000 bp (1 Mb). For designs targeting the whole genome or large regions, you can ignore this warning.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the listed lines. If they are intended (for example, a large linkage region), you can ignore this warning. Otherwise, correct them.

<a id="bed011"></a>
### BED011: Interval names are unique

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} {are} used for more than one interval (for example, "{name}" is used {times} times). Since results are typically reported by name, duplicate names may cause these results to be merged or overwritten.

**How it works**

This check is only performed when column 4 (name) is present. Empty names and the placeholder '.' are ignored. Different exons of the same gene often use the same name, and this is acceptable in some cases.

**Suggested fix**

> Ensure that names are unique (for example, by adding exon numbers). Alternatively, if duplicate names are intentional, ignore this warning.

## Sample sheet

<a id="ss001"></a>
### SS001: Required columns are present and filled in

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} Without them, the workflow cannot determine which samples and files to process.

**How it works**

The schema is located at src/ngs_preflight/schema/samplesheet.yaml. Required columns are sample_id, fastq_1, and fastq_2 for FASTQ rows (fastq_2 is not required for rows where fastq_1 is a BAM or CRAM file, and the column may be omitted entirely). Optional columns are sex, family_id, paternal_id, maternal_id, library_id, and lane. Column names must match exactly and are case-sensitive. Close matches such as 'Sample ID' will be reported as hints. Blank cells in required columns will also be reported.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="ss002"></a>
### SS002: Sample IDs are unique

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} on more than one row without a different lane number (for example, "{sample}" on lines {lines}). 2 different samples with the same ID cannot be distinguished, and their results would be merged or overwritten.

**How it works**

The same sample_id is allowed in multiple rows only if a 'lane' column is present. In these rows, lane values must be non-empty and distinct (i.e. the same sample is sequenced across multiple lanes). All other cases are considered duplicates.

**Suggested fix**

> Assign a unique ID to each sample. If the same sample was sequenced across multiple lanes, add a lane column and assign the corresponding lane number to each row.

<a id="ss003"></a>
### SS003: Sample IDs use safe characters

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} not allowed (for example, "{example}"). Sample IDs may contain only letters, digits, underscores, and hyphens, up to {max_length} characters. Spaces, slashes, and other symbols cause problems with file names and many workflow tools.

**How it works**

Schema pattern is ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ and the maximum length is 64. Empty IDs are reported by SS001 and are not reported here.

**Suggested fix**

> Change sample names using only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscores (_), and hyphens (-).

<a id="ss004"></a>
### SS004: Read files exist and are readable

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** the read-file folder (`--reads-dir`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} listed in the sample sheet could not be found or opened (for example, "{path}" for sample "{sample}"{why}). The run would fail as soon as it tried to read them.

**How it works**

Relative paths are resolved against --reads-dir, while absolute paths are used as provided. Paths expressed as URLs (s3://, gs://, https://, ...) are skipped because they cannot be validated. Files with a size of 0 bytes are considered unreadable.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the file names for spelling errors, and confirm that the files have been copied to the folder specified by --reads-dir. Upload any missing files.

<a id="ss005"></a>
### SS005: No file is listed twice

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} listed more than once (for example, "{path}", used by {users}). Reads from one file would be counted under several samples, or the same reads would be used as both read 1 and read 2.

**How it works**

Paths are compared in their recorded form after slash normalization. If the same file appears in 2 rows or in both fastq_1 and fastq_2 within 1 row, this is reported.

**Suggested fix**

> Check that each sample references its own files. If you created a new row by copying another row, update the file names in that row.

<a id="ss006"></a>
### SS006: Read 1 and read 2 files pair up

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} not look like matching read 1 / read 2 pairs (for example, sample "{sample}": {why}). Mispaired files make alignment fail or produce meaningless results, often only after hours of computation.

**How it works**

File names are compared after R1/R2 (or _1/_2) is replaced with a placeholder. If both files are readable (--reads-dir), the first 100 read names are compared. This comparison uses the first token of each header and ignores a trailing /1 or /2. Files without an R1/R2 marker pass the name test.

**Suggested fix**

> Confirm that fastq_1 contains the read 1 file and fastq_2 contains the read 2 file. Check that these files came from the same sequencing run and that neither has been renamed or swapped.

<a id="ss007"></a>
### SS007: Compressed files are intact

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** the read-file folder (`--reads-dir`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} damaged or incomplete (for example, "{path}": {why}). An interrupted download or copy is the usual cause, and it makes runs fail partway through.

**How it works**

This is a quick check and does not provide full validation. For every .gz/.bam file, it checks the gzip signature and the header, and that the first 4 MiB can be decompressed. BGZF files (.bam, bgzip FASTQ) must contain the 28-byte end-of-file marker. Other gzip files of 32 MiB or less are decompressed in full and their CRC is verified. Larger non-BGZF gzip files cannot be shown to be complete at low cost, so only their beginning and end are checked.

**Suggested fix**

> Copy or download the file again, and compare its checksum (for example, md5sum) with the checksum provided by the sender.

<a id="ss008"></a>
### SS008: Sex values are from the allowed list

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {count} not in the list of allowed values (for example, "{value}" for sample "{sample}"). Downstream steps and the sex check need a recognized value.

**How it works**

Accepted values are male/m/1, female/f/2, and unknown/u/0/NA/n/a/'.' (case-insensitive). A blank value is also allowed and indicates unknown sex. This vocabulary is defined in src/ngs_preflight/schema/samplesheet.yaml.

**Suggested fix**

> Use male, female, or unknown (or M, F, U, or 1, 2, 0), or leave the cell blank.

<a id="ss009"></a>
### SS009: Family relationships are consistent

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} The pedigree is used for relatedness checks and by analyses which take the pedigree into account, so an inconsistent pedigree can give incorrect results.

**How it works**

Every non-empty paternal_id / maternal_id must match the sample_id in another row, and no sample may be its own father or mother. Blank values, 0, '.', NA, n/a, and none indicate no parent record.

**Suggested fix**

> Add a row for each parent (if a parent is not included in this submission, leave the corresponding parent cell blank). Also confirm that no individual is listed as their own parent.

## Reference compatibility

<a id="ref001"></a>
### REF001: Reference, BED and reads agree on naming and genome build

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} {consequence}

**How it works**

Naming format is determined from the primary chromosomes (1-22, X, Y, M, with or without 'chr'). A BAM header is compared to the reference sequence. If no reference sequence is available, the BED is compared to the BAM header instead (the BED comparison to the reference sequence is reported in detail in BED003).

Genome build is determined by comparing contig lengths. Different lengths indicate different genome builds even for the same chromosome (for example, chr1 has a length of 249,250,621 bp in GRCh37 and chr1 has a length of 248,956,422 bp in GRCh38). When --expected-build is specified, the reference's own genome build is also identified from its sequence lengths and compared to the expected build. Only the BAM header is read. See REF003.

**Suggested fix**

> {fix}

<a id="ref002"></a>
### REF002: Reads and reference list the same chromosomes

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** a reference (`--reference`).

**Message shown to the customer**

> {problem} GATK and DeepVariant currently accept this situation. However, stricter tools may not accept it, and reads on chromosomes absent from the reference sequence will be ignored.

**How it works**

Compares the chromosome names in the BAM header to those in the reference sequence. Reports names present in the BAM but absent from the reference sequence. Also reports primary chromosomes (1-22, X, Y, M) present in the reference sequence but absent from the BAM header. These differences are not reported when the naming style differs (this is described in REF001).

**Suggested fix**

> Align reads to the same reference sequence you submitted, or provide the reference sequence used to align them. For an intentionally partial BAM, confirm that its header lists only the chromosomes included in that BAM.

<a id="ref003"></a>
### REF003: Read-file header could not be inspected

**Severity:** INFO. **Needs:** -.

**Message shown to the customer**

> {reason} This file was not included in the reference sequence compatibility checks (REF001, REF002).

**How it works**

BAM headers are read directly. This version does not check CRAM headers. BAM files whose headers cannot be parsed are reported here (integrity problems are reported by SS007).

**Suggested fix**

> No action is required. If compatibility matters, confirm this file's reference using another method.

## Sample identity (optional, uses somalier)

<a id="id001"></a>
### ID001: No two samples are the same person

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> Samples "{a}" and "{b}" have nearly identical genotypes (relatedness {relatedness:.2f}, where 1.0 indicates the same individual). 2 different sample IDs must not refer to the same individual. Either the same sample was submitted under 2 names, or a sample mix-up occurred.

**How it works**

somalier relate compares genotypes at about 17,000 common sites. All pairs with different sample IDs and relatedness above 0.9 are reported. This check cannot distinguish identical twins from sequencing the same individual twice.

**Suggested fix**

> Confirm with the submitter which sample each file actually belongs to. If one is a duplicate of the other, assign them the same sample ID and different library or sequencing lane values, or exclude one.

<a id="id002"></a>
### ID002: Declared parent and child are related as expected

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> The sample sheet lists "{parent}" as the {role} of "{child}", but their genetic relatedness is only {relatedness:.2f} (about 0.50 would be expected for a parent and child). Either the pedigree in the sample sheet is incorrect, or the samples have been mixed up or mislabelled.

**How it works**

For all declared parent-child pairs where both samples are present, relatedness calculated by somalier relate must be within 0.35-0.65 (expected value of 0.5). Even if the father and son are swapped in the sample sheet, they remain a parent-child pair. However, this swap can usually be detected because the relationship with the other parent would no longer meet the criteria.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the paternal_id / maternal_id columns against the supplied pedigree information. If the sample sheet is correct, ask the laboratory to check the sample labels.

<a id="id003"></a>
### ID003: Unrelated samples are unrelated

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> Samples "{a}" and "{b}" are not listed as related in the sample sheet, but their genomic relatedness is {relatedness:.2f} (close to 0 for unrelated individuals). They may be relatives which the sample sheet does not mention, or the sample sheet may be incomplete.

**How it works**

Sample pairs with relatedness between 0.2 and 0.9 are reported if their relationship is not recorded in the sample sheet. Pairs within the same family_id, parent-child pairs, and sibling pairs (samples which share a declared parent) are never reported. Samples absent from the sample sheet are not reported.

**Suggested fix**

> If these individuals are related, add the family_id and parent columns. If these individuals are expected to be unrelated, check with the laboratory whether a sample mix-up has occurred.

<a id="id004"></a>
### ID004: Declared sex matches the data

**Severity:** ERROR. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> The sample sheet lists "{sample}" as {declared}, but the data suggest {inferred} (X chromosome heterozygosity and X/Y read depth). Either the sex recorded in the sample sheet is incorrect, or the sample has been mixed up.

**How it works**

somalier infers sex per sample using heterozygous calls on chrX and relative depth on chrX and chrY. A discrepancy is reported when the sample sheet says male or female and somalier infers the opposite sex. Samples declared unknown or whose sex somalier cannot determine are not reported. This determination requires enough sites on chrX/chrY, and very low coverage may prevent a result. somalier uses read depth, which VCF input does not have. When somalier makes no call, sex is inferred from chrX instead. If heterozygous variants account for less than 5% of non-reference variant calls, the sample is classified as male. If this proportion is greater than 25%, the sample is classified as female. Other cases, including samples with fewer than 20 such sites, are unknown.

**Suggested fix**

> Check the sex recorded for this sample. If the sample sheet is correct, ask the laboratory to confirm that no sample mix-up occurred.

<a id="id005"></a>
### ID005: Enough informative sites for an identity call

**Severity:** WARN. **Needs:** `--identity`, somalier, `--sites`.

**Message shown to the customer**

> Only {sites:,} sample identity sites were readable for "{sample}" (we consider {low} sites the minimum for reliable results). With so few sites, the relatedness and sex results for this sample may be incorrect, so treat its sample identity checks as unconfirmed.

**How it works**

Informative sites are sites which somalier classifies as homozygous for the reference allele, heterozygous, or homozygous for the alternate allele. This warning is displayed when their number is below 5,000 (about 28% of the 17,766 sites in the standard hg38 list). Typical causes include low coverage, targeted panels which do not cover these sites, or a lack of hom-ref records in the VCF.

**Suggested fix**

> Use data with higher sequencing depth or whole-genome or whole-exome files to verify sample identity. For targeted panels, consider whether verifying sample identity is meaningful.
